title: Telemetry Braid: lightweight request carrier shim for multi-protocol trace propagation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Implement a minimal, polyglot request carrier shim ("Telemetry Braid") that stitches together multiple trace propagation formats with zero or near-zero per-request overhead. The shim will live as a thin middleware/adapter in Redwood SDKs and as an opt-in HTTP/gRPC edge middleware to: 1) normalize incoming headers (W3C traceparent, b3, x-cloud-trace-context, legacy-x-rw-trace) into a single internal carrier, 2) maintain cross-service trace id continuity when requests travel through gateways or legacy clients, and 3) provide a safe fallback mapping when full trace context fields are missing.

Scope & goals: 
- Minimal runtime overhead (<0.03ms median per request added in microbenchmarks).
- Polyglot support: Node, Python, Go SDKs and edge Go proxy middleware.
- Compatibility-first: preserve existing headers, but prefer W3C traceparent internally when present.
- Deterministic fallback: if only legacy Redwood header present, synthesize traceparent preserving trace id and sampling.
- Non-invasive: no forced OpenTelemetry dependency for consumers; expose optional OTEL bridge adapter.

Out-of-scope for MVP: automatic baggage encryption, full OTLP exporter changes, and deep log enrichment beyond trace_id injection.
acceptance_criteria: SDK adapters (Node/Python/Go) expose Telemetry Braid middleware and pass unit tests
Edge Go middleware can normalize headers and add internal carrier header without changing upstream headers
End-to-end test shows trace continuity between legacy client -> proxy -> backend with correct trace_id correlation
Performance regression <1% p50 on synthetic workload compared to baseline
Docs and migration guide published (Confluence) and linked in SDK READMEs
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Kaur: Initial spike complete. PoC normalizes traceparent and b3 into internal header 'x-rw-telemetry' and passes handshake tests. Measured overhead ~0.028ms/core in Node microbench.

2026-03-04 - Mateo Garcia: Implemented Go middleware prototype in rw-proxy. Observed a 0.05ms median increase on the edge under 10k RPS (p95 slightly higher). Added batching micro-optimizations to header parsing to reduce allocs.

2026-03-06 - Design review (Lina Chen): Approved header name and compatibility strategy. Requested explicit prohibition on modifying incoming W3C traceparent header; we should only synthesize an internal carrier.

2026-03-07 - Security (Omar Patel): Flagged risk around copying untrusted 'baggage' fields. Decision: do not forward arbitrary baggage by default; add opt-in config 'braid.forward_baggage' and a whitelist in SDKs.

2026-03-09 - QA (Jules Martin): Added E2E test scenario with legacy mobile client. Found an edge where sampling flag lost during proxy->backend hop. Added deterministic sampling propagation patch to shim.
2026-03-11 - Mateo Garcia: Opened PRs for Node and Go. Node PR includes a compatibility layer for Express/Koa. Performance benchmarks attached. Requesting an owner for final code review: @s-reilly.

2026-03-12 - s-reilly (code review): Suggested moving the parse/format utilities into a shared 'telemetry-util' package to avoid duplication across SDKs; asked for non-regression tests for header preservation.
notes: Trade-offs considered: heavy OTEL dependency would give richer context but increases binary size and cold-start overhead; chosen approach keeps runtime very small and provides an OTEL bridge adapter for teams that want it. Rollout plan: feature-flagged in SDKs -> enable for internal services -> staged rollout to customers with opt-in console toggle. Monitoring: create an alert for % of requests that have synthesized traceparent > 0.1% (indicates misconfigured clients).
